chunks: And by his chain, he said: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
Three (things) I fear for my community after me: straying after recognition, and the deceptions of trials/strife, and the lustful desires of the belly and the private part.

key_terms.شَهْوَةُ الْفَرْجِ: Lustful desire of the private part (sexual desire)
key_terms.مَضَلَّاتُ الْفِتَنِ: Deceptions or paths of misguidance within trials/strife

ai.seo_question: What are the three things the Prophet feared for his Ummah after him?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) warns against three specific spiritual dangers: apostasy after certainty, the confusion of fitnah, and unchecked carnal desires. Shia scholars emphasize that 'shahwat al-batin wa al-farj' refers not merely to physical lust but to the dominance of the lower self (nafs) over reason, which leads to the loss of divine knowledge. This triad highlights the internal struggle required to maintain faith in the post-Prophetic era.

en.hubeali:
And by his chain, 
‘He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘

Three (things) I<sup>saww</sup> a fearing these off upon my<sup>saww</sup> community from after me<sup>saww</sup> – the straying after the recognition, and the deceptions of the strife, and the lustful desires of the belly and the private part’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his sources of narrators who have said the following: “The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘
There are three things about which I am afraid for my followers after me: misguidance after recognition of the truth, confusion because of mischief and the desires of stomach and genital organs.’”
